subject.title: Feature: Message continuation marker for batched input (cost savings)

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic marker-controlled inbound continuation contract, treat existing debounce and collect modes as the supported batching answer, or require a plugin/API seam before marker buffering exists?
rationale: The request adds public config and changes how inbound fragments become one model-visible session turn, so automation cannot safely choose marker syntax, timeout, stripping, media, command, transcript, and typing semantics.

options.title: Design Generic Ingress Continuation
options.body: Add one opt-in core or SDK-backed continuation contract with typed config, schema/docs, marker stripping, timeout behavior, and tests across inbound debounce, queue, transcript, and typing behavior.

options.title: Document Existing Batching As Sufficient
options.body: Keep marker syntax out of core and steer users toward messages.inbound debounce plus messages.queue.collect for cost-reduction batching.

options.title: Require Plugin/API Seam First
options.body: Defer the feature until a typed channel or plugin ingress hook can implement marker buffering without growing core message config directly.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Ingress Continuation
recommendation.body: Add one opt-in core or SDK-backed continuation contract with typed config, schema/docs, marker stripping, timeout behavior, and tests across inbound debounce, queue, transcript, and typing behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across shared inbound debounce policy, current schema/config, queue-adjacent behavior, and prior product-review context.
